title: Homophily and transitivity in dynamic network formation
abstract: arXiv:2609.14049v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In social and economic networks linked agents often share connections in common. There are two competing explanations for this phenomenon. First, agents may have a structural taste for transitive links - the returns to linking may be higher if two agents share a common connection. Second, agents may assortatively match on unobserved attributes, a process called homophily. We study parameter identifiability in a simple model of dynamic network formation with both effects. Agents form, maintain, and dissolve links over time to maximize utility. The return to linking may be higher if agents share connections in common. A pair-specific utility component allows for arbitrary homophily on time-invariant agent attributes. We derive conditions under which it is possible to detect the presence of a taste for transitivity in the presence of assortative matching on unobservables. translated_title: 动态网络形成中的同质性与传递性
translated_abstract: 在社会和经济网络中，相互连接的主体往往拥有共同的连接关系。对这一现象存在两种竞争性解释：第一，主体可能对传递性连接存在结构性偏好——当两个主体拥有共同连接时，建立连接的回报可能更高；第二，主体可能基于不可观测的属性进行分类匹配，这一过程被称为同质性。本文研究了一个同时包含这两种效应的简单动态网络形成模型中的参数可识别性问题。主体随时间推移建立、维持和解散连接以实现效用最大化。当主体之间拥有共同连接时，建立连接的回报可能更高。一个针对连接对的特定效用分量允许在时间不变的主体属性上存在任意形式的同质性。我们推导出了在存在不可观测属性分类匹配的情况下，能够检测出传递性偏好存在的条件。
tldr: 本文研究了同时包含同质性与传递性偏好的动态网络形成模型中的参数可识别性问题，推导出了在不可观测属性分类匹配存在的情况下识别传递性偏好所需的条件。
en_tdlr: This paper studies parameter identifiability in a dynamic network formation model with both homophily and transitivity, deriving conditions under which a taste for transitive links can be identified despite assortative matching on unobservables.
